homepage.title: A pizza shop should be able to keep its menu and take orders direct.
homepage.lede: Pizza4People is a public proof of one small thing: the customer can discover a restaurant through a public registry, but the menu and the order go straight to the shop. The first live shape is intentionally narrow: direct pickup orders and simple pay-at-pickup before anything broader.
homepage.notice: Status: public protocol proof with a controlled live-pilot path, not broad production infrastructure. Just Eat Takeaway.com announced 30 April 2026 as the date its Danish operations would conclude.
homepage.press_heading: The story is ready to discuss. The live restaurant pilot is still being prepared.
homepage.press_lede: Pizza4People can be covered now as a public protocol proof responding to a real market exit. The careful wording is important: this is not a finished replacement for Just Eat, not a delivery company, and not a production restaurant network yet.

press_facts.title: What is public now
press_facts.body: Public main repo, public proof note, readable protocol/spec docs, schemas, reference code, and an independent node interop kit.

press_facts.title: Where to start on GitHub
press_facts.body: Start with the repo README, the proof note, SPEC.md, and the release notes.

press_facts.title: What is being tested next
press_facts.body: Several independent people can build their own nodes and check whether they interoperate before the first real pickup-order pilot goes live.

press_facts.title: What changed in the module layer
press_facts.body: The public repo now includes replaceable customer menu modules, internal mock payment modules, operator workflow modules, and a money contract where prices are integer minor units with an explicit node currency.

press_facts.title: What the first pilot means
press_facts.body: One restaurant-owned node, one primary registry, one backup registry, and explicit operator approval before live pickup orders.

press_facts.title: Where to verify
press_facts.body: The public repo is the conservative story branch. The proof site and the broader protocol-family framing remain the narrowest public places to verify what exists now.

press_facts.title: Press kit
press_facts.body: Open the press kit in Danish or English. PDF exports remain artifacts; the HTML kits are the maintained source.

homepage.story_heading: Start with the restaurant, not the marketplace.
homepage.story_body: The point is not to launch another giant food app. The point is to let a pizzeria keep the basic connection: its own menu, its own direct order endpoint, and a small pickup-first flow it can actually control. This public proof is the first step toward that.
homepage.one_sentence: The customer finds the shop through a public directory, but the menu and order go straight to the shop.

plain_demo.title: Find a pizzeria
plain_demo.body: The client asks a registry for nearby restaurant nodes and can discover a public proof node now.

plain_demo.title: Open the menu
plain_demo.body: The menu is fetched from the restaurant node, either as structured items or through a photo-map view of a paper menu fixture.

plain_demo.title: Send a test order
plain_demo.body: The order goes directly to the node. In the public proof this is a test order; in the pilot it becomes explicit restaurant-approved pickup ordering.

plain_demo.title: Break the primary registry
plain_demo.body: Discovery still works through a backup registry because the node announced itself to both.

homepage.problem_heading: A market exit exposes who owns the basic connection.
problem_body: Closed marketplaces can be useful, but they also concentrate discovery, customer access, order intake, and commercial terms in one place. When a platform leaves, restaurants and customers should not have to rebuild the basic contact layer from zero.
For a journalist, the story is not "new pizza app". The story is whether basic local commerce should depend on one private discovery and ordering silo at a time.

proof_steps.title: Discover
proof_steps.body: A client asks a registry for nearby pizza nodes. This is the phone book part.

proof_steps.title: Fetch menu
proof_steps.body: The client requests the menu directly from the selected node. The registry is not the menu owner.

proof_steps.title: Send direct order
proof_steps.body: The client sends the order directly to the node. Public proof orders remain test orders until a restaurant operator explicitly enables live mode.

proof_steps.title: Fail over
proof_steps.body: If the primary registry disappears, discovery can still work through a backup registry.

homepage.takeaway_heading: This is not a replacement for Just Eat today. It is a working argument for an open base layer.
homepage.takeaway_body: A company can still build delivery, payments, support, loyalty, analytics, or hosting on top. The point is that no single company should have to own discovery, identity, and the first restaurant-customer contact for the system to work.
proves: Public discovery can be separated from order handling.
Menu and test order requests can go directly to the node.
A node can sign announcements with its own key.
A registry can record public identity events without holding node private keys.
Menu prices can carry explicit currency and integer minor-unit amounts without P4P doing currency conversion.
does_not_prove: No broad production restaurant network yet.
No real payment processing, delivery, CVR verification, or certification yet.
No claim that registries automatically synchronize.
homepage.trust_body: The current P4P direction is node-owned identity. A node signs its own announcement. A registry verifies the node signature, records an identity event, and can later publish signed snapshots. The registry does not need the restaurant's private key.
homepage.proof_gate_heading: Selective outreach can point to the public repo. Broad launch still waits for the live-pilot dry run.

proof_gate.label: client fetches menu directly from node
client sends a direct test order
backup registry discovery works after primary failure
public GitHub repo explains the public proof path clearly
independent node interop kit is published
live pilot node has completed end-to-end dry run

roadmap: Public protocol. Clean GitHub repository, readable proof note, spec, schemas, reference implementation, and a short GitHub reading path.
Controlled restaurant pilot. One real restaurant node, primary registry, backup registry, and explicit operator approval before live orders.
Module manifests. Provider declarations with data-access boundaries, including menu, order, status, kitchen, stock, print, and internal mock payment modules.
Trust and federation. CVR binding, signed snapshots, scoped registries, and reviewable trust claims.
homepage.footer_status: Public protocol proof. Controlled live pilot next.

dk.kicker: Open protocol proof / kontrolleret live-pilot næste
dk.headline: Ikke endnu en pizzaapp.
dk.lede: Pizza4People er et offentligt proof af en lille model: en pizzabutik kan beholde sin egen menu, tage direkte pickup-ordrer og starte med betaling ved afhentning, mens kunden stadig kan finde butikken gennem en åben registry.
dk.quote: Den korte historie: Når en platform forlader et marked, bør restauranter og kunder ikke miste den grundlæggende digitale forbindelse, fordi forbindelsen aldrig var deres.
dk.why_now_heading: Just Eat forlader Danmark. Det gør platformafhængighed synlig.
why_now_body: Just Eat Takeaway.com bekræftede i deres newsroom, at driften i Danmark slutter den 30. april 2026. Det er ikke bare en nyhed om én app. Det er et synligt eksempel på et dybere spørgsmål: hvem ejer det digitale kontaktlag mellem restauranter og kunder?
Pizza4People svarer ikke med et nyt lukket marketplace. Det svarer med et smallere spørgsmål: kan den basale discovery, menuadgang og ordreafsendelse være åben protokol i stedet for platformsilo?
journalist_bullets: En pizzabutik kan beholde menuen og tage direkte pickup-ordrer.
Discovery kan være public uden at platformen ejer ordreflowet.
Det er ikke produktionsklar restaurantdrift endnu.
Næste trin er uafhængige node-tests og en kontrolleret restaurantpilot.
dk.source_note: Kilde: Just Eat Takeaway.com Newsroom, "Just Eat Takeaway.com intends to cease operations in Denmark", opdatering 14. april 2026.
dk.system_heading: Registry finder. Node ejer. Kunden taler direkte med node.
dk.layers_heading: Åben base først. Kommercielle services ovenpå.
dk.status_heading: Hvad der er publiceret, og hvad der testes næste.
current_status_items: Public GitHub repository med spec, schemas og referencekode
Reference registry, client, demo-node og pilot-node foundation
next_test_items: 2-3 uafhængige personer bygger hver sin node.
Hver node testes med samme checker.
Alle noder annoncerer til samme registry.
Client finder noderne og sender direkte testordre.
Første restaurantpilot kører pickup-only og kun med eksplicit live-mode.
dk.verification_heading: Andre kan bygge deres egen node og teste mod kontrakten.
verification_body: Det vigtigste ved proofet er ikke, at én referenceimplementation virker. Det vigtige er, at andre kan implementere samme lille kontrakt og stadig interopere.
Derfor er der publiceret et implementer-kit og en dependency-free checker, som tester minimumsfladen for en node.

en.kicker: Open protocol proof / controlled live pilot next
en.headline: Not another pizza app.
en.lede: Pizza4People is a public proof of a small model: a pizza shop can keep its own menu, take direct pickup orders, and start with pay at pickup while the customer can still discover the shop through a public registry.
en.quote: The short version: When a platform leaves a market, restaurants and customers should not lose the basic digital connection because that connection was never theirs.
en.why_now_heading: Just Eat is leaving Denmark. Platform dependency becomes visible.
why_now_body: Just Eat Takeaway.com has confirmed that operations in Denmark end on 30 April 2026. This is not only a story about one app. It exposes a deeper question: who owns the digital contact layer between restaurants and customers?
Pizza4People does not answer with another closed marketplace. It asks a narrower question: can basic discovery, menu access and order submission be an open protocol instead of a platform silo?
journalist_bullets: A pizza shop can keep its own menu and take direct pickup orders.
Discovery can stay public without the platform owning the order flow.
It is not production-ready restaurant infrastructure yet.
The next step is independent node tests and a controlled restaurant pilot.
en.source_note: Source: Just Eat Takeaway.com Newsroom, "Just Eat Takeaway.com intends to cease operations in Denmark", update dated 14 April 2026.
en.system_heading: Registry discovers. Node owns. Client talks directly to node.
en.layers_heading: Open base first. Commercial services on top.
en.status_heading: What is public now, and what gets tested next.
current_status_items: Public GitHub repository with spec, schemas and reference code
Reference registry, client and node foundation
next_test_items: Two or three independent people build their own nodes.
Each node is tested with the same checker.
All nodes announce to the same registry.
The client discovers nodes and sends direct test orders.
The first restaurant pilot runs pickup-only and only with explicit live mode.
en.verification_heading: Others can build their own node and test against the contract.
verification_body: The important part is not that one reference implementation works. The important part is that others can implement the same small contract and still interoperate.
The public repository includes an implementer kit and a dependency-free checker for the minimum node surface.
en.press_angles_heading: Three ways to cover the story without overstating it.

press_angles.title: Open web / protocol
press_angles.body: Can local commerce get an open base layer before commercial services are added?

press_angles.title: Foodtech / restaurant
press_angles.body: The restaurant's digital identity, menu and order endpoint can stay with the restaurant.

en.status_line: Accurate status line: Pizza4People is a public open-protocol proof. The next step is independent node interoperability and a controlled live pilot. It is not a finished restaurant platform.
